slots.title: ISM manufacturing 55.2 est. at 2 p.m.
slots.body:
ISM Manufacturing PMI for August is on the calendar at 2:00 p.m.
ET.

Consensus: 55.2.

Prior reading: 55.6.

A reading above 50 means more factories report growth than contraction—that is the plain-English line on the index.

Same release window: JOLTs job openings for July.

Estimate: 7.3M openings.

Previous: 7.4M (7.359M in the feed).

That pair ties factory demand to how many roles employers still had unfilled.

U.S. equity benchmarks finished Aug. 31 lower ahead of the prints:
- $SPY proxy ^GSPC -0.3% to 7,685.01
- ^DJI -0.7% to 53,185.90

Which number do you watch first—factory PMI or job openings?

slots.title: Brent at $91.13 after Hormuz strike
slots.body:
Brent crude closed at $91.13, up 0.7% in the feed.

Headline driver: a tanker struck while transiting eastbound through the Strait of Hormuz, with renewed U.S.–Iran tension in the same news cycle.

Oil-exposed proxies in the cross-asset snapshot moved with crude:
- Brent (BZUSD): $91.13, +0.7%
- $USO: $133.70, +3.1%

The CBOE Volatility Index finished at 14.92, up 3.4% on Aug. 31.

Major U.S. indexes were down modestly into month-end:
- ^GSPC: 7,685.01, -0.3%

What do you track when shipping headlines hit—Brent spot or an ETF like $USO?

slots.title: Hang Seng -1.1% as Shein debuts
slots.body:
Hang Seng: 25,292.29, -1.1% in the overseas block.

Fast-fashion retailer Shein began trading in Hong Kong after a long-awaited IPO, with multiple outlets reporting shares lower in early dealing.

CNBC cited roughly a 7% drop in the debut session; WSJ framed regulatory headwinds and slowing sales against a prior valuation near $66 billion.

Regional benchmark context in the same feed:
- ^N225: 66,050.33, -0.4%
- ^FTSE: 10,824.26, +0.3%

U.S. session date in the pack: 2026-08-31, with ^IXIC -0.1% to 26,370.89 at the close.

When a mega IPO stumbles overseas, do you look at the local index or sector peers first?

slots.title: California utility shares fall on liability fight
slots.body:
$EIX closed down 23.1% at 53.98.

$PCG closed down 20.1% at 13.27.

Coverage pointed to California lawmakers pushing back on a proposal to limit how much utilities owe after wildfire damage.

Both names were among the session’s largest liquid decliners by percentage.

Which part of the wildfire-liability debate are you tracking closest?

slots.title: Brent above $91 as Hormuz tanker report hits tape
slots.body:
Brent settled at 91.13, up 0.7% on the session.

Headlines cited a tanker hit by projectiles transiting the Strait of Hormuz and renewed focus on shipping risk in the region.

Large U.S. oil names moved with crude:

- $XOM +2.7% to 160.98
- $CVX +2.1% to 206.15

The oil ETF proxy $USO rose 3.1% to 133.70.

How are you reading the link between shipping headlines and energy stocks this week?

slots.title: SAIC EPS $3.01 beats $2.31 estimate
slots.body:
$SAIC reported EPS of 3.01 versus an estimate of 2.31.

Revenue came in at 1.88B versus an estimate of about 1.76B.

The stock closed up 1.8% at 128.22.

Day range: 127.10 to 141.18.

Do you follow defense and government IT names around the print, or mostly the megacaps?

slots.title: US cash session recap — Aug. 31, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed at 7,685.01, down 0.3% (26.75 points).
The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.7%, finishing at 53,185.90.
The Nasdaq Composite was off 0.1% at 26,370.89.
The Russell 2000 fell 0.5% to 2,956.45.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 3.4% to 14.92, with an intraday high of 15.48.

Brent crude settled at 91.13 (+0.7%).
Gold futures were little changed at 4,483.80 (+0.1%).
The U.S. oil fund proxy $USO rose 3.1% to 133.70.
Bitcoin was up 0.1% at 78,647.15.
The dollar proxy $UUP slipped 0.2% to 28.12.
EUR/USD held near 1.16.

Treasury yields in the injected snapshot (dated 2026-08-28) showed the 10-year at 4.7% and the 2s10s spread at 0.39.

On the calendar, the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index for August printed at 11.6 versus a 0.7 estimate (prior 1.3).
Three- and six-month bill auction results were also released late in the session.

Sector averages on Nasdaq showed healthcare up about 1.3% and real estate up about 1.1%.
Communication services lagged, down about 1.0%.
Consumer cyclical names averaged up about 0.9%; energy down about 0.6% despite gains in several large oil stocks.

California utility shares led large percentage declines after coverage of lawmakers balking at wildfire liability limits: $EIX -23.1% to 53.98 and $PCG -20.1% to 13.27.

Energy majors moved higher with crude: $XOM +2.7% to 160.98 and $CVX +2.1% to 206.15.

Among megacaps, $TSLA rose 5.5% to 367.95.
$AMZN fell 2.5% to 259.77.
$GOOG fell 2.2% to 335.41.
$NVDA gained 1.5% to 220.78.
$META was down 1.0% at 572.34.

$SAIC reported results with EPS 3.01 vs 2.31 estimated and revenue above the estimate; the stock closed up 1.8% at 128.22.

Overseas indexes in the data included the Hang Seng down 1.2% and the Nikkei 225 off 0.4%; the FTSE 100 was up 0.3%.

slots.title: August payrolls print Friday at 12:30
slots.body:

That bundle is the main hard read on how many people employers added and what workers are being paid.

What part of the report do you track first — the headline job count or the wage line?

slots.title: Factory activity gauge due Monday at 2 p.m.
slots.body:
ISM Manufacturing PMI (Aug) — Monday, Sep. 1, 2:00 p.m.
ET.

Estimate: 55.2.
Prior: 55.6.

The index summarizes orders, production, and employment at U.S. factories; above 50 points to expansion, below 50 to contraction.

Same release window includes ISM Manufacturing Employment (estimate 52.5, prior 52.8) and ISM Manufacturing Prices (estimate 72.0, prior 71.1), which track hiring and input costs on the factory floor.

Job openings for July (JOLTs) are also scheduled Monday at 2:00 p.m., estimate 7.3M, prior 7.359M.

Which Monday print do you watch closer — the PMI headline or job openings?
